environmentalPersistence: Low — rapidly degraded by light (photolysis) and soil microbes; half-life hours to days

lowDose.description: Promotes cell elongation in stems, stimulates lateral root initiation, enhances apical dominance. Positive growth effects — taller stems, more developed root system, healthy leaf expansion.

highDose.description: Epinasty, ethylene induction, growth inhibition, root necrosis at extreme doses, leaf abscission, oxidative stress.

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Biphasic — low dose promotes elongation; high dose strongly suppresses via ethylene induction
morphologicalEffects.leafSize: Increased at low dose; reduced at high dose
morphologicalEffects.leafCurl: Strong downward epinasty at high doses — mediated through ethylene induction
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Moderate at high doses — ethylene-driven turgor loss
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Moderate at high doses — ethylene-mediated chlorophyll degradation
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Moderate at high doses — root tip necrosis most prominent
morphologicalEffects.pigmentation: Mild anthocyanin increase under stress doses
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Strongly stimulated at low dose (lateral root initiation); inhibited at high dose
morphologicalEffects.stemThickness: Increased at low dose; reduced at high dose
morphologicalEffects.branching: Inhibited at low dose (apical dominance); released at high dose as apical tissue damaged
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Apical young leaves most sensitive to epinasty; old leaves show chlorosis first

physiologyEffects.chlorophyllReduction: Moderate at high doses — secondary to ethylene induction
physiologyEffects.photosyntheticRate: Maintained at low dose; reduced at high dose
physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Mildly increased at low dose; reduced at high dose
physiologyEffects.waterUptake: Enhanced at low dose; impaired at high dose
physiologyEffects.nutrientTransport: Enhanced at low dose via improved vascular development; disrupted at high dose

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Mild at low dose; moderate at high dose — partly via induced ethylene
molecularEffects.lipidPeroxidation: Mild to moderate at high doses

microbiomeEffects.diversityReduction: Mild — auxin alters root exudate composition
microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Mixed — some PGPR produce IAA themselves; exogenous IAA can suppress or stimulate depending on strain

temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: 1–2 weeks — IAA degrades quickly; recovery faster than most chemicals
temporalDynamics.sensitization: Auxin signaling involves receptor degradation; repeated high-dose exposure can desensitize

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Low dose: deeper green, taller plants. High dose: yellowing, curled epinastic leaves
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Apical meristem and young leaves (epinasty); roots (inhibition)
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Downward from apex at high dose
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Moderate — IAA conjugate and oxindole metabolite signature; strongest in stem tissue
visualSimulation.microbiomeParticles: Near-normal at low dose; mildly disrupted at high dose
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: Good recovery — re-greening and straightening within 1–2 weeks of removal

synergies.synergyNote: Auxin + GA3 produces the strongest elongation response — synergistic on heightSuppress axis in reverse (growth promotion); combined high dose accelerates ethylene induction
synergies.antagonismNote: Cytokinins antagonize apical dominance maintained by auxin. Ethylene reduces auxin sensitivity in roots.

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Endogenous plant hormone — present in all vascular plants; synthetic analogs (2,4-D) used as herbicides
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Rooting powders for cuttings, fruit thinning, synthetic analog 2,4-D as selective herbicide
educationalContext.humanToxicity: IAA itself — low toxicity. Synthetic auxin herbicides (2,4-D) — moderate concern; possible carcinogen
educationalContext.climateLink: Auxin distribution altered by temperature changes — relevant to understanding growth responses under warming
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Both — used in home horticulture rooting powders
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Why plants grow toward light (phototropism) — auxin is the molecule behind it. One of the most fundamental concepts in plant biology.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Herbicide development, crop yield optimization, understanding tropisms
